picks.editorial_note: A $334 million grant from Schmidt Sciences to build a new national supercomputing system is one of the largest single investments in AI research infrastructure this year, dramatically expanding capacity for scientific discovery nationwide.
picks.title: NCSA Joins the Schmidt Science Computing Network to Expand Advanced Computing for Scientific Discovery

picks.editorial_note: UC Berkeley and Berkeley Lab's entry into the same Schmidt Science Computing Network, establishing the Berkeley Science AI Platform at NERSC, shows the initiative is building a coordinated national HPC backbone rather than a single isolated grant.
picks.title: UC Berkeley, Berkeley Lab collaboration with Schmidt Science Computing Network will Provide High Performance Computing for Cutting-Edge Research - NERSC: National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center

picks.editorial_note: An AI model designed a bacteriophage used in the first-ever treatment of a patient with an antibiotic-resistant infection, a landmark proof that generative AI can produce functional biological therapeutics with direct clinical impact.
picks.title: This time, the virus is on the patient’s side. AI helped design it

picks.editorial_note: An independent machine-learning technique confirmed the iconic Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87 black hole in a Nature publication, a significant validation of one of astrophysics' most famous results using AI methods.
picks.title: New CSIRO technique confirms iconic black hole image

picks.editorial_note: A fresh $19 million state grant to Texas Tech for a next-generation AI-and-simulation computing cluster signals growing state-level investment in building regional semiconductor and AI research capacity.
picks.title: Texas Tech Receives $19 Million Grant to Further Semiconductor Innovation | Texas Tech Now

picks.editorial_note: Imperial College London and France's CNRS launched a joint international laboratory applying AI to multiscale metabolism research, an example of deepening transatlantic academic collaboration aimed at global health challenges.
picks.title: Metabolism, AI and global health: Imperial and France's CNRS celebrate launch of joint laboratory

picks.editorial_note: University of Amsterdam legal scholars' critique that the EU's proposed Cloud and AI Development Act doesn't go far enough to reduce dependence on US cloud providers highlights a live policy fight over European digital sovereignty.
picks.title: 'EU plan for cloud and AI falls short on digital autonomy'

picks.editorial_note: A Michigan Tech-UCLA study showing AI models need far less training data than assumed to predict materials' electronic structures could substantially lower the cost and speed of AI-driven materials discovery.
picks.title: Less Data, Faster Discovery: Researchers Rethink AI’s Role in Developing New Materials

picks.editorial_note: The University of Kansas's new master research agreement with cybersecurity firm SOFTwarfare reflects a growing pattern of universities formalizing direct industry partnerships around trustworthy and secure AI systems.
picks.title: KU establishes partnership with Kansas-based AI and cybersecurity company

picks.editorial_note: Indiana University's new Applied Research Center coordinates university-wide AI expertise for government and industry national security work, illustrating academia's expanding role in AI-driven security priorities.
picks.title: Indiana University expands national security research partnerships through Applied Research Center
